evidence.text: On the July call management said Q4 would include a one-time refund of tariffs paid 'for our other cost items', and raised the FY26 restaurant-level margin guide to about 18.5% with that refund inside it. Courts ordered IEEPA duties refunded to all importers of record with interest (March 2026), and CBP opened a refund process on 2026-04-20. So the refund is real, but its size is undisclosed, and it covers non-food items because food is likely imported by others.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior refund on this name. On other names in this repo, tariff refunds landing in the quarter split by the direction of guidance: two rose double digits and two fell double digits.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is inside the 18.5% margin guide and the $0.20 EPS bar. The only unpriced part is the size. If the refund also covered food-ingredient duties paid as importer of record, it could be several million dollars against Q4 net income of about $2.4M (12.2M shares x $0.20). The market would then be anchoring EPS above $0.25, and it is not.
evidence.independence: The legal mechanism is independent of the company: https://taxprofblog.aals.org/2026/04/21/ieepa-tariff-refund-process-begins/. The company-level size is unsourced.

evidence.text: Tariff relief for FY27 is limited. The Supreme Court ended IEEPA duties in February 2026, but a Section 122 global tariff ran 2026-02-24 to 2026-07-24, and Section 301 duties with a 12.5% floor on goods of Japan replaced it the same minute. Kura's imported ingredients therefore still carry about 12.5% against 15% under IEEPA, not zero. Separately, Asian fishing-fleet fuel costs more than doubled after the Strait of Hormuz closed in April 2026. Both bear on the FY27 COGS line, which management expected to run about 30% of sales in FY26 (+200bp from tariffs).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The tariff-driven COGS rise was named in the Q1 FY26 print (2026-01-07, stock +16.7% anyway on comps and traffic) and the Q2 print (2026-04-07, -17.8% on the CFO exit and Hormuz fish-fuel costs).
evidence.why_not_priced: The tariff regime is public. What is unpriced is how much of a 'tariff relief' margin story survives in the FY27 guide. Management said it aims for a 20% margin 'regardless of tariff relief', so a guide that assumes relief would surprise on the upside and one that assumes the 12.5% floor would not. This is macro-to-company transmission and the company has not confirmed it.
evidence.independence: Hormuz fish-fuel costs: https://www.tridge.com/news/kura-sushi-usas-17-nasdaq-slide-shows-toughe-awxcvjgq (2026-04-09). Section 122 expiry: https://borderbuddy.com/trade-tariff-news/section-122-is-out-section-301-is-in. Shares the COGS line with the margin finding below, which points the other way and rests on a different statement.
